column1: # What the odi-oss image does with each config key. Hand-written, per image,
# and the reason the UI shows 21 keys instead of 184: a key with no row here is
# read by nothing on this image. It stays in the store, and in backups and
# restores, because the config partition is shared with the stock firmware in
# the other slot, which does read it -- but it is not offered for editing.
# apply    what applying costs, shown beside the key:
#            live      takes effect at once, no interruption (a VLAN key: omcid
#                      rebuilds the connections in place, the ONU stays in O5)
#            restart   a daemon restarts; the fibre service stays up
#            internet  applied without a reboot, but the fibre service drops
#                      while it is (omcid deactivates the ONU, clears its MIB
#                      and the ONU ranges and is provisioned again)
#            reboot    only at the next boot, which also drops the service
# action   what the page runs to apply it: network (apply.sh network), omci
#          (apply.sh omci), syslog, ntp, reboot, or none (the daemon reads the key
#          each time it uses it, nothing to run). confd reports the actions a
#          save needs. omci sends SIGHUP to omcid, which rereads the store: for
#          a live key it rebuilds in place, for an internet key it re-registers
# pair     shown read-only and written together with the named key
# reader   what on the image reads it
# note     why it costs what it does
# unset    the value the image uses while the key is absent, one of its
#          options; the page shows that option selected. Required for every
#          key with an option list: the image always does something, so the
#          page never offers or shows "not set" for one.
# Source of truth for the classes: odi-oss docs/SETTINGS.md. scripts/check-schema.py
# checks every name against keys.tsv and every class and action against the lists

column5: omcid, at each software download step
column6: Read each time the OLT starts, activates or commits a software download, so a change is in effect at once and nothing is applied. An odi-only key, kept in odi.conf.

column5: omcid, at each Reboot from the OLT
column6: Read each time the OLT sends a Reboot, so a change is in effect at once and nothing is applied. An odi-only key, kept in odi.conf.
An odi-only key, kept in odi.conf. Changes what omcid answers the OLT for classes it does not model, so applying re-registers the ONU and the OLT provisions it again with the new answers.

column5: omcid, at start and on SIGHUP
column6: An odi-only key, kept in odi.conf: empty removes it. Applying re-registers the ONU so the OLT reads the entities again.
Needs a reboot: the MAC is set on eth0 and its host port with the links down, before br0 exists, and doing that live would cut every way in mid-change.
Applying deactivates the ONU, writes the new serial into the PON MAC (the driver accepts it only while the ONU is deactivated) and ranges it again; the OLT sees a new ONU. A reboot applies it too.
Applying restarts syslogd (init respawns it with the new address); the fibre service is not touched.
Applying restarts ntpd (init respawns it with the new server); the fibre service is not touched.
